matterhorn.story: Traveller, may the Matterhorn greet you as a large, near-symmetric pyramidal peak in the Pennine Alps, straddling the border between Switzerland and Italy and rising 4,478 metres above sea level. Its four steep faces, separated by the Hörnli, Furggen, Zmutt and Leone ridges, overlook Zermatt to the northeast and Breuil-Cervinia to the south, with Theodul Pass just to the east. Called the “Mountain of Mountains” and an emblem of Switzerland and the Alps, it has been described as the most beautiful mountain in the world and claimed to be the most photographed. Remember that its first ascent in 1865 from Zermatt, led by Edward Whymper, ended in disaster when four of the seven climbers died during the descent, and over 500 alpinists have died on the Matterhorn, making it one of the deadliest peaks in the world.
matterhorn.name: Matterhorn

dufourspitze.story: For a traveller in the Alps, the Dufourspitze rises as the highest peak of Monte Rosa, an ice-covered mountain massif, and the highest mountain of both Switzerland and the Pennine Alps. It is also the second-highest mountain of the Alps and Western Europe, after Mont Blanc, located between Switzerland and Italy, though the peak itself lies wholly in Switzerland. Its summit, once called Höchste Spitze, was first reached on 1 August 1855 from Zermatt by a party of eight climbers led by three guides, and on 28 January 1863 the Federal Council renamed it Dufourspitze in honor of Guillaume-Henri Dufour. Just 80 m east and only 2 metres lower, the Dunantspitze was renamed in 2014 in honor of Henry Dunant.
dufourspitze.name: Dufourspitze

chiesa-vecchia-macugnaga.story: Come to the alpine village of Macugnaga, at the foot of Monte Rosa, and find the Old Church, or Chiesa Vecchia. This small church was built in the second half of the 13th century and dedicated to the Blessed Mary of the Assumption. It was the first parish church of Macugnaga, surrounded by a cemetery where many alpinists, climbers, and writers have been buried or honoured. In the Dorf, where Walser people used to live in huts made of larch trunks, the church stands beside The Old Linden, an ancient tree approximately 700 years old.
chiesa-vecchia-macugnaga.name: Chiesa Vecchia, Macugnaga

dent-d-h-rens.story: For a traveller, the Dent d'Hérens is a 4,173 m mountain in the Pennine Alps, lying on the border between Italy and Switzerland a few kilometres west of the Matterhorn. Along its east ridge are Punta Bianca, Punta Carrel with its subpeak Punta Maquignaz, and the significant Punta Maria Cristina, while the Aosta hut at 2,781 m is used for the normal route. It takes its name from the Val d'Hérens further north, though older and local names—including Dent Blanche, Dent de Rong, and Dent d'Erins—caused confusion until the official names used today were fixed with the completion of the Dufour map in 1862. The mountain stands on the main alpine watershed between Valais and Aosta Valley, rising on the Swiss side above the Zmutt Glacier in the remote valley of Zmutt and lying north of Cervinia on the Italian side.
dent-d-h-rens.name: Dent d'Hérens

breithorn.story: Traveller, high on the main chain of the Alps, roughly halfway between the Matterhorn and Monte Rosa and east of the Theodul Pass, you will find the Breithorn — literally “broad horn” — whose highest peak rises to 13,661 ft / 4,160 m on the border between Switzerland and Italy. Much of this Pennine Alps massif is glaciated, with subsidiary peaks all east of the main summit: the Central Breithorn, the western Breithorn Twin, the Gendarm and the Roccia Nera, while Zermatt and St-Jacques are the nearest settlements. Because the Klein Matterhorn cable car takes climbers from Zermatt to over 3,820 m as a starting point, the Breithorn is considered the most easily climbed 4,000 m Alpine peak. Remember too that the standard route runs along the SSW flank from the Italian side, continuing over a glacial plateau before climbing to the summit on a 35-degree snow slope, where caution matters near cornices or in bad weather.
breithorn.name: Breithorn

zermatt.story: Welcome to Zermatt, a town at the upper end of Mattertal, 1,620 m high and at the foot of Switzerland’s highest peaks. It is famed as a mountaineering and ski resort of the Swiss Alps, and while it was predominantly agricultural until the mid-19th century, the tragic first ascent of the Matterhorn in 1865 was followed by a rush on the surrounding mountains and the construction of many tourist facilities. Its name comes from the alpine meadows, or matten, and appeared first as Zur Matte; older names include Praborno or Prato Borno, with Prato also meaning meadow. Though its year-round population is about 5,800, there may be several times as many tourists in Zermatt at any one time.
zermatt.name: Zermatt

bouquetins.story: Traveller, the Bouquetins—or Dents de Bouquetins—are a multi-summited mountain of the Alps between Switzerland and Italy, and their name is French for Alpine ibices. They form a ridge composed of several summits above 3,600 metres, the highest being 3,838 metres, and they are the highest mountain on the main watershed of the Pennine Alps west of the Dent d'Hérens. At the western base of the mountain is the Refuge des Bouquetins, owned by the Swiss Alpine Club, so this place holds both a high ridge and a shelter for your warm story.
bouquetins.name: Bouquetins

gornergrat.story: When you ride from Zermatt on the Gornergrat rack railway, the highest open-air railway in Europe, you climb almost 1,500 m through Riffelalp and Riffelberg to the last stop on this rocky ridge of the Pennine Alps. Between the railway station and the summit, the Kulm Hotel sits at 3,120 m, with two astronomical observatories installed in its towers in the late 1960s and the Stellarium Gornergrat hosted in the Gornergrat South Observatory. From this ridge between the Gornergletscher and Findelgletscher, you can take in panoramic views of 29 mountains above 4,000 m, including Dufourspitze, Liskamm, Matterhorn, Dom, and Weisshorn. Nearby, on the west side of the Gorner Ridge by Rotenboden railway station, Riffelhorn rises at 2,928 m.
gornergrat.name: Gornergrat
